items.t: Chapter 2 (al-bāb al-thānī): On breaking and spreading (al-kasr wa- l-basṭ) and the ordering of the operations according to the [proper] times and hours

Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him, in the understanding of His secrets, and in His providential care — that of the sun and the moon God, exalted is He, has spoken and has made mention of them in His Mighty Book, in His saying, exalted is He: "and the sun and the moon, each swimming in an orbit" (Q 21:33). This is because the moon, when it alights in the mansion of al-Naṭḥ— which is the letter (alif) — is [then] governed by the secret of the alif. So when it descends into that mansion, the spiritual force (rūḥāniyya) of the alif is disclosed from that mansion, and wrath appears throughout the parts of the world, and most of all among the noble and the great ones of the people of this world. Every one of created beings finds subjugation and contraction within his inward being, according to the mode proper to his human rank; and whoever examines this closely will find it so. A man ought therefore to keep still in that hour, to employ his bodily members in the worship of God, exalted is He, and in abundant remembrance of Him, and to keep to ritual purity in that hour. In it souls are contracted, so that a man does not know the cause of his contraction and becomes astonished within himself. That is because the alif is the first of the ranks of the units among the numbers and among the letters, so that it has no like; and for that reason it is through it that disquiet befalls the lower world. Understand that. In it, too, is the embittering (tanghīṣ) of whomever you wish to embitter among the people of this world and its most eminent, of the sort given to tyranny and arrogance; for it is suited to embittering him and to [drawing] profit from him — this because of the heat and dryness in the letter alif, on account of which the disquiet occurs and souls are contracted when the moon alights in it, and because of the heat and dryness in al-Naṭḥ; for it is the decan (wajh) of the Red One (al-Aḥmar, Mars), and the Red One is hot and dry, of the nature of fire, burning by its own kind.

So, if you invoke in it with hot, dry names of its own nature — when al-Naṭḥis rising upon the eastern horizon and the moon is in it — and you write the letter 111 times upon red copper, or upon iron, or upon a potsherd of red earthenware, in the name of the one you wish to embitter, and you place it in the fire after you have suffumigated it with something of its own kind, in which there is heat, such as khazaf (earthenware) and qaḍāb and the like; and you invoke with the names 111 times — these being the numbers that fall to the spreading (basṭ) of the alif. As for the names with which you invoke against him: it is that you take the letters of the name of the person mentioned, whom you wish to embitter and constrict, and spread them out, and look to see which of the natures predominates in his name — heat, or dryness, or cold, or moisture. Then you take /fol. 8v./ those hot and dry letters from his name and set them before you upon a tablet, and you add to them the letters of Mars (al-Mirrīkh), of al-Naṭḥ, and of the moon (al-qamar), and out of them you compose one of the names of God, exalted is He, and you invoke with it the number of times stated, and you gather your entire resolve (himma) upon crushing and subduing him.
An example of this: Zayd and ʿAmr. You set down the letters, separated and spread out, thus:

. These are fourteen letters. Of them, fiery are; earthy are ;of the hot-and-moist letters there are three, namely; and of the cold-and-moist letters there is one, namely.The hot letters, counted with their repetitions, were four:. The dry, with their repetitions, were six letters:

.The hot-and-moist are three, which are those written above; and the cold-and-moist is likewise as written, without repetition. So reckon up the fourteen letters: what predominates in these letters is heat and dryness. There came out for us, then, from the names of God, exalted is He, these. You say: I adjure you, O Samsamāʾīl, the [angelic] king, by Him who created you and fashioned you aright, and made you a light within your sphere, and singled you out with His might and bestowed it upon you — [I adjure you] that you be my helper in what I desire of you. For I have set you in power over So-and-so son of So-and-so, that you take vengeance upon him, and demolish his senses, and mingle with the heat of Mars in the heat of his nature, and stir up in him a fiery heat with which you crush his joints, and constrict with it his heart and his inward being, and destroy his mind; and that you bring down upon him the angels of chastisement and the fire of Mars, and set in motion against him fires and headache and all the other pains — by the right of Mars and the malefic influence and fire that is in it, and by the right of your mansion, lofty in measure, of dry heat, that takes vengeance upon the tyrannical oppressors and the transgressing despots. And send the spiritual beings of Mars, the masters of fire and chastisement and subjugation and affliction, against the spirit of this despot, transgressor, arrogant and tyrant; and let them give the chastisement of vengeance power over his body, and set over his inward being the secret of subjugation and wrath and vengeance. Truly I have adjured you by al-Qawī (the Strong), al-Muḥīṭ (the All-Encompassing), al-Ṭābiq (the Conforming), al-Ḥayy (the Living), al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), al-Nūr (the Light), al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), al-Muqaddim (the Promoter), al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer), the Outpourer of lights and the Giver of secrets; and by the right of the fire and the sparks and the Red Planet; and by God, al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing): answer, O angels, obedient and swift, to the names of the Lord of the Worlds!
[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in source]
And you write together with it the five-by-five square (al-mukhammas).
Fig. 4

Know, my brother — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that the letter alif has an airy wafq; to it belongs the planet Mars, and its servant-spirit is al-Aḥmar (the Red One). It is a letter of powerful effect: when you multiply it by its like, it manifests obedience; and it is the limit of the units. Know, too, that this noble letter has power in the operative deployment (taṣrīf) of all the remaining letters, for it is like the father. Understand this. As for its occult properties: if you want it for love, you write it in this form, as we have set it out for you, in a /fol. 9r./ fortunate hour; and if you blend the name of the person for whom you are performing the operation together with the letter of the square, it is more beautiful and stronger in its effects. You say: I adjure you, O Samsamāʾīl, and your servant-spirits and your helpers of the celestial and of the terrestrial order, and all the servant-spirits of the letter alif; I adjure you that you hear and obey and stir up and disquiet — 252 — by the right of that by which I have adjured you, and by the right of the letter alif and the secrets that God, exalted is He, has sent down within it, upon which none looks save the lofty ones who know God; and by the right of abjad and the occult properties it contains: [I adjure you] that you answer with obedience to that to which I have summoned you, and by that with which I have adjured you. And judge by analogy with this whatever operations and acts are suited to it, and you will succeed, if God, exalted is He, wills, and your operation will succeed.

This is the wafq of the letter alif, whose secret and excellence are renowned among the learned. And if you want it for operations of corruption, do as we have mentioned and you will attain your object. God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Fig. 5

The second of the mansions is the mansion of al-Buṭayn, and to it belongs the letter (bāʾ). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it, by the leave of God, exalted is He, a spiritual power fit for wrath and for what has been mentioned above. In it medicine is drunk, and in it the great ones, the sons of this world, and the kings of the earth are stirred into motion, because this decan of Aries is the second, and it is the decan of the sun; in it falls the sun's exaltation, at six of its degrees, on the fourth day of April. The sun is benefic, save that it is hot and dry, of the nature of Mars. Because of its benefic quality and its exaltation in this decan, one works in it for acceptance and for gaining access to kings, for whatever you want of them and whatever you seek from them in it — for your needs will be granted. One works in it, too, for acts of love, for acceptance, and for the attraction of hearts; and strive by means of it toward whatever calls for that. It is also suitable for performing the philosophical arts (al-ṣināʿāt al-ḥikmiyya) and the golden elixirs and their regimen (tadbīr). /fol. 9v./

The third of the mansions is the mansion of al-Thurayyā, and to it belongs the letter (jīm). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it, by the command of God, exalted is He, a spiritual power compounded of heat and moisture, and a middling benefic influence, good for travel, for mingling with the nobles and gaining access to them, and to the great ones, the masters of this world, and the people of knowledge; for al-Thurayyā is an assembly of many stars, and therefore assembly with those we have mentioned is good in it. It has a mighty wafq, which is made during its exaltation and is carried, and with it one goes in upon the nobles; whoever carries it attains his object from them, and they love him and obey him in his affair, and none opposes him in what he wants and seeks. By it Abū Jaʿfar al-Barmakī was favoured with al-Rashīd, and obtained from him everything he wanted. This is the form of its layout, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.
Fig. 6

The fourth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Dabarān, and to it belongs the letter (dāl). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it an evil spiritual force; in it you perform what befits it of evil operations and corruption, and whatever of that suits it.

The fifth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Haqʿa, and to it belongs the letter (hāʾ). When the moon alights in it, there is disclosed from it, by the leave of God, exalted is He, a spiritual force compounded with middling motion. Perform in it works of good, and some of the contrary as well.

The sixth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Hanʿa, and to it belongs the letter (wāw). When the moon alights in it — and it is a fortunate mansion — it is fit for producing affection and union between those who hate one another and those who are estranged, because there descends from it a spiritual force that aids /fol. 10r./ works of righteousness, piety, and success.

The seventh of the mansions is the mansion of al-Dhirāʿ, and to it belongs the letter (zāy). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it a good spiritual force that aids in medical treatments; and in it an opening is granted to the practitioners of devotional seclusion in the retreat-cells (zawāyā), and whoever is absorbed in contemplation has disclosed to him a secret from the Kingdom (malakūt). It is good for devotional seclusion (iʿtikāf) and for the seeking of the Reality, and it is favourable in all operations.

The eighth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Nathra, and to it belongs the letter (ḥāʾ). When the moon alights in it, there is disclosed from it a spiritual force that gives no aid toward good; in it you perform the chapters of corruption.

The ninth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Ṭarf, and to it belongs the letter (ṭāʾ). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it a spiritual force whose action is evil, like the preceding one.

The tenth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Jabha, and to it belongs the letter (yāʾ). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it a spiritual force mixed between good and evil; in it one performs what befits it.

The eleventh of the mansions is the mansion of al-Zubra, and to it belongs the letter (kāf). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it a spiritual force apt for the increase of provision and for the seeking of needs; in it you perform what befits it.

The twelfth of the mansions is the mansion al-Ṣarfa, and to it belongs the letter (lām). When the moon alights in it, there descends from it a spiritual force mixed for good and evil; in it you perform what befits that.

The thirteenth of the mansions is the mansion of al-ʿAwwāʾ, and to it belongs the letter (mīm). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a mixed spiritual force (rūḥāniyya mumtazija). Let nothing be undertaken in it except embarking upon the sea — nothing else.

The fourteenth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Simāk, and to it belongs the letter (nūn). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a spiritual force that gives no aid toward good; so let nothing whatsoever be performed in it.

The fifteenth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Ghafr, and to it belongs the letter (sīn). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a beneficent spiritual force that aids every undertaking, of this world and of the next. So do in it whatever you wish, and your operation will succeed.

The sixteenth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Zubānā, and to it belongs the letter (ʿayn). When the moon alights in it there comes down from it, by the leave of God — exalted is He — a mixed spiritual force; so undertake nothing in it save for good.

The seventeenth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Iklīl, and to it belongs the letter (fāʾ). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a spiritual force that gives no aid to the works of good. Perform in it such of the righteous works as are fitting, and you will prosper.
The eighteenth of the mansions, which is the mansion of al-Qalb, and to it belongs the letter (ṣād). There descends from it a spiritual force that aids in all good.

The nineteenth of the mansions, which is the mansion of al-Shawla, and to it belongs the letter (qāf). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a mixed spiritual force; so undertake nothing in it pertaining to the needs of this world.

The twentieth of the mansions is the mansion of al-Naʿāʾim, and to it belongs the letter (rāʾ). When the moon alights in it, God — exalted is He — sends down from it a mixed spiritual force, manifest, which purifies hearts and gladdens souls. It is good for everything one takes in hand /fol. 10v./ of the affairs of this world and of the next.

The twenty-first of the mansions, which is the mansion of al-Balda, and to it belongs the letter (shīn). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a spiritual force that gives no aid toward good; so undertake nothing in it for good.

The twenty-second of the mansions, which is the mansion of Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, and to it belongs the letter (tāʾ). When the moon alights in it there descends from it, by the leave of God — exalted is He — a mixed spiritual force; it is fit for nothing of the affairs of this world, and there is no profit in undertaking anything in it.

The twenty-third of the mansions is the mansion of Saʿd Bulaʿ, and to it belongs the letter (thāʾ). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a mixed spiritual force; it is fit for nothing, and in undertaking anything there is neither profit nor harm.
The twenty-fourth is the mansion of Saʿd al-Suʿūd, and to it belongs the letter (khāʾ). When the moon alights in it, God — exalted is He —
sends down a spiritual force that is beneficent, good for undertakings, temperate in nature. Do in it whatever you wish.

The twenty-fifth is the mansion of Saʿd al-Akhbiya, and to it belongs the letter (dhāl). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a spiritual force that is felicitous and aids all praiseworthy works, and aids concord, love, and affection.

The twenty-sixth of the mansions, which is the mansion of Farʿ al-Muqaddam, and to it belongs the letter (ḍād). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a felicitous spiritual force that aids all deeds of good. So do in it what you will of the works of good.

The twenty-seventh of the mansions, which is the mansion of al-Farʿ al-Muʾakhkhar, and to it belongs the letter (ẓāʾ). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a mixed spiritual force which blocks endeavour and the means of attainment in it.

The twenty-eighth of the mansions, which is the mansion of al-Rishāʾ, and to it belongs the letter (ghayn). When the moon alights in it there descends from it a spiritual force that is fair, good, and praiseworthy, which aids the learned in the pursuit of knowledge; supplication in it is answered, and righteous works performed in it grow and increase.

So consider, my brother, what benefits God — exalted is He — has established by means of the letters. And since it is of the letters that the speech of God — exalted is He — is composed, and by them the names of God — exalted is He — are known, and through them His address from

God — exalted is He — is understood, the meaning that lies in their inward reality is the spiritual force that descends from the mansions. And just as the Mighty Qurʾān contains verses of mercy and verses of chastisement, so to mercy there belong angels of good fortune with respect to him who is shown mercy through them, and to the verses of chastisement angels of ill fortune for him who is chastised through them; and there are verses that entail both promise and threat — and these are what is denoted by the "mixed spiritual force". This holds only with respect to man; with respect to the angels there is no deficiency, for they are pure good. In man there is pure good, which is the faith that subsists in him; and pure evil, which is the unbeliever; and mixed good, which is the disobedient believer, of whom God — exalted is He — said: And others have confessed their sins; they have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. It may be that God will turn to them in forgiveness (Q 9:102). And this is a likeness /fol. 11r./ that is plain. By these secrets within the letters the cycles have revolved upon the point, through the stages of composition, until the day of emergence into this world: every mansion, every spiritual force, and every letter gathered within the quantity of the point in forty days, and so on to the last of the mansions. Thus with the last of the letters, together with the last of the spiritual forces, are gathered the auspicious and the inauspicious influences. Were it not for this distribution among the letters and this revolution of the celestial sphere, man would not know the causes of felicity that come from the auspicious influences, nor the causes of wretchedness that come from the inauspicious ones, nor the causes of mixture that come from divergence. All of that is already determined in the innate constitution of the son of Adam.

Faṣl. And since these mansions are distributed among the twelve zodiacal signs, that His wisdom might be manifested in them, the letters were twelve, in six segmentations (taqṭīʿāt), namely the letters of lā ilāha illā Allāh, thus:— so they are twelve letters, according to the number of the twelve zodiacal signs, and thus it stands in every sign. And since among the zodiacal signs some are fixed and some are turning (munqalib), so likewise among these twelve letters some are fixed and some are turning: affirmation is fixed, and negation is turning — from being to the non-being from which it comes. And the secret of these letters is that the sphere of the moon revolves by means of them, for the moon is nearer to the earth than any other body, while the letters are nearer to us than the moon, since they are implanted in the innate constitution of every human being. The letters have already been mentioned in connection with the mansions, so I need not repeat them. Everything increases with the waxing of the moon and diminishes with its waning, by the wisdom of its ordering and the knowledge of its ranks. Do you not see how the darkness increases, and other things too? And since the seven planets (al-sabʿ al-darārī) are the sun, the moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury, God — exalted is He — placed in them the secret of guidance, according to His words — exalted is He — And it is He who made the stars for you, that you might be guided by them through the darknesses of land and sea (Q 6:97). In them, then, lies the secret of "making", which is a species of power.
[Fig. 7 — table of the twenty-eight letters in abjad order, seven rows of four; cells as in source, each row read from right to left]

For among His Most Beautiful Names is al-Jāʿil (the One who makes and appoints), according to His words — exalted is He — who appoints the angels as messengers (Q 35:1), and His words — exalted is He — Indeed I am appointing upon the earth a vicegerent (Q 2:30). And the powers of these seven planets are drawn from the powers of the segmentations hidden within lā ilāha illā Allāh; they derive from these most holy celestial realities.
Now I shall alert you to the letters that are hot, dry, cold and moist. The hot are seven letters:. The moist are seven letters:
. The cold are seven letters: .And the dry are seven letters:

Fire, then, combines heat and dryness; air combines moisture and heat; water combines cold and moisture; and earth combines dryness and cold. Thus there enter in the four natures already mentioned, namely yellow bile, blood, phlegm, and black bile: yellow bile is the nature of fire, hot and dry; blood is the nature of air, hot and moist; phlegm is the nature of water, cold and moist; and black bile is the nature of earth, cold and dry. /fol. 11v./ The effect of this has become manifest to the eye, in that certain names, when written, suppress fever — namely the cold names, such as His name al-ʿAdl (the Just), which is powerful. These cold and dry letters you set into a seven-fold square (musabbaʿ), thus. And likewise certain names suppress bitter cold (zamharīr) — namely the burning, yellow-bilious ones.

Faṣl: in which we mention the auspicious and the inauspicious times and their hours, and which of them accord with good and which with evil

Sunday. The first hour belongs to the Sun: work in it for acceptance and for entering in upon kings and rulers; it is also suitable in it to put on new clothes. The second hour belongs to Venus, and it is a blameworthy hour: do nothing in it, of any of the things whatsoever. The third hour belongs to Mercury: travel in it, and write in it for inclining the affections, for love, for acceptance, and the like. The fourth hour belongs to the Moon: neither sell nor buy in it; it is fit for nothing. The fifth hour belongs to Saturn: work in it for separation, hatred, and enmity, and the like. The sixth hour belongs to Jupiter: seek in it your needs from kings, sultans, and the great. The seventh hour belongs to Mars: do nothing in it at all, for it is inauspicious. The eighth hour belongs to the Sun: work in it for all your needs, for it is suitable for all needs and affairs, and it is an exceedingly auspicious hour. The ninth hour belongs to Venus: write in it for travel, for the drawing of people, for the inclining of hearts, for love-workings, and the like. The tenth hour [belongs to Mercury]: make in it talismans and seal-rings and the like. The eleventh hour [belongs to the Moon]: do in it all that you wish, for it is a praiseworthy hour. The twelfth hour belongs to Saturn: work in it nothing but harmful things, such as separation and hatred and the like.

Monday. The first hour belongs to the Moon: it is suitable for love-workings, for the binding of tongues, and for the drawing of hearts. The second hour belongs to Saturn: it is of benefit for travel and for the success of one's needs. The third hour belongs to Jupiter: it is suitable for marriage, for moving house, for the drawing up of the marriage contract, and for litigation. /fol. 12r./ The fourth hour belongs to Mars: it is suitable for evil operations, such as haemorrhage, nosebleed, sickness, destruction, and the like. The fifth hour belongs to the Sun: it is suitable for the fulfilment of needs, for love-workings, and for arousals. The sixth hour belongs to Venus: it is suitable for the fulfilment of needs and for the attraction of hearts. The seventh hour belongs to Mercury: it is suitable for the making of talismans and other such things. The eighth hour belongs to the Moon: it is suitable for marriage and for reconciliation between those at enmity. The hour

The ninth hour belongs to Saturn: it is suitable for separation, for removal, for hatred, and the like. The tenth hour belongs to Jupiter: it is suitable for acceptance, for love, for the binding of tongues, and for reconciliation between those at enmity. The eleventh hour belongs to Mars: write in it for enmity, for hatred, for haemorrhage, for the shedding of blood, and for other such things. The twelfth hour belongs to the Sun: it is suitable for the binding of tongues and for the inclinings of affection.

Tuesday. The first hour belongs to Mars: the operation in it is for hatred, for corruption, for separation, for haemorrhage, for sicknesses and diseases. The second hour belongs to the Sun: do nothing in it at all. The third hour belongs to Venus: it is suitable for the betrothal of women and for marriage. The fourth hour belongs to Mercury: write in it for the attracting of customers, and for selling, buying, and trade. The fifth hour belongs to the Moon: do nothing in it, for it is blameworthy, inauspicious, and obstructed. The sixth hour: writing is suitable in it for binding, for ophthalmia, for sicknesses, and the like. The seventh hour belongs to Jupiter: work in it whatever you wish of the inclinings of affection, of love-workings, and the like. The eighth hour belongs to Mars: work in it whatever you wish of haemorrhage, of the casting of blood, and of sicknesses. The ninth hour belongs to the Sun: it is suitable for the binding of women and for arousals. The tenth hour belongs to Venus: do nothing in it, for it is not praiseworthy. The eleventh hour belongs to Mercury: it is suitable for the obstructing of journeys, for hindrance from marriage, and the like. The twelfth hour belongs to the Moon: it is suitable for the operations of hatred, of corruption, of removal, of evil, and of divorce, and the like.

Wednesday. The first hour belongs to Mercury: it is suitable for acceptance, for love-workings, and the like. The second hour belongs to the Moon: do not attempt any of the operations in it, for it is blameworthy. The third hour belongs to Saturn: it is suitable for the working of diseases, of haemorrhage, of the drying-up [of waters], and the like. The fourth hour belongs to Jupiter: work in it whatever you wish of the operations of good, for it is excellent. The fifth hour belongs to Mars: beware in it of quarrelling with people and of evil work, /fol. 12v./ for it is blameworthy. The sixth hour belongs to the Sun: it is suitable for travel by land and by sea; and write in it whatever you wish of the operations of good. The seventh hour belongs to Venus: work in it likewise whatever you wish, for it is praiseworthy in its effects. The eighth hour belongs to Mercury: it is suitable for the crying of children, for the writing of protective amulets against the [evil] eye and the [evil] glance, and the like. The ninth hour belongs to the Moon: do nothing in it whatsoever, for it is bad. The tenth hour belongs to Saturn: it is good for entering into the presence of sultans and the great. The eleventh hour belongs to Jupiter: write in it the awfāq for meeting rulers, for litigations, and the like. The twelfth hour belongs to Mars.

Thursday. The first hour belongs to Jupiter: work in it for the attracting of provision and of customers, and for acceptance among people. The second hour belongs to Mars: draw no blood in it, and do not work in it the bindings and the haemorrhages. The third hour belongs to the Sun: never travel in it; and write in it for acceptance, for love, and the like. The fourth hour belongs to Venus: work in it for love-workings, for marriage, and for other than that. The fifth hour belongs to Mercury: binding is suitable in it, for women and for men. The sixth hour belongs to the Moon: travel by land and by sea is suitable in it, and it is suitable for every operation you desire of the operations of good. The seventh hour belongs to Saturn: beware of litigation in it; it is suitable for meeting the men of the pen. The eighth hour belongs to Jupiter. The ninth hour belongs to Mars: it is suitable for meeting emirs and for the operations of corruption. The tenth hour belongs to the Sun: seek in it your needs from sultans, emirs, soldiery, and the holders of office. The eleventh hour belongs to Venus: write in it for acceptance, for love, and for other such things. The twelfth hour belongs to Mercury: never do any operation in it.

Friday. The first hour belongs to Venus: work in it the arousals for women, their attraction and their love, and reconciliation between a woman and her husband. The second hour belongs to Mercury: write in it all the talismans. The third hour belongs to the Moon: do nothing in it at all, for anyone. The fourth hour belongs to Saturn: it is suitable for the drying-up of springs and wells. The fifth hour belongs to Jupiter: one writes in it for acceptance with women. The sixth hour belongs to the Sun: write in it for meeting sultans and for the fulfilment of needs. The seventh hour belongs to Venus: work in it the arousals, the inclinings of affection, the betrothal of women and their marriage. The eighth hour belongs to Mercury: work in it all the operations and acts — your operation will succeed, for it is blessed. The ninth hour /fol. 13r./ belongs to the Moon: work in it separation and removal, for it is swift of response. The tenth hour: do no operation in it save the drying-up of springs, of waters, and of wells. The eleventh hour belongs to Jupiter: do no operation in it. The twelfth hour belongs to Mars: travel in it and seek your needs and whatever aims you desire, for it will succeed, since it is blessed and excellent.

Saturday. The first hour belongs to Saturn: work in it whatever you wish of acceptance-workings and love-workings, for Saturn has none but this fortunate hour on this day — provided it be the beginning of the month, with the crescent moon in its increase. But if it be the end of the month, then on Saturday, in the hour of Saturn, one writes all the inauspicious operations. Understand, and you will be rightly guided, for we have made plain to you the clear course of the way. The second hour belongs to Jupiter: write in it for reconciliation between those at enmity. The third hour belongs to Mars: work in it for separations, for hatreds, and for all the operations of evil and corruption. The Properties of the Planets
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 18

The planet Zuḥal (Saturn) has an extremely dry and cold nature; its element is earth, its gender is female, and it is reckoned as diurnal. This planet is the executioner of the heavens, and it rises in the seventh heaven. It is nahis (malefic) and is the greatest of the inauspicious planets.
The planet Mushtarī (Jupiter) has a moist and hot nature; its element is fire, its gender is male, and it is reckoned as diurnal.
This planet is the judge (kadi) of the heavens, and it rises in the sixth heaven. It is said (benefic) and is the greatest of the auspicious planets.
The planet Mirrīkh (Mars) has an extremely dry and hot nature; its element is fire, its gender is male, and it is reckoned as nocturnal.
This planet is the lord (bey) of the heavens, and it rises in the fifth heaven. It is nahis and is the lesser of the inauspicious planets.

The planet Shams (the Sun) has a dry and hot nature; its element is fire, its gender is male, and it is reckoned as diurnal. The planet Shams is the [I 19] sultan of the heavens, and it rises in the fourth heaven. It is said and is the greatest of the luminous planets.
The planet Zuhra (Venus) has a dry and cold nature; its element is earth, its gender is female, and it is reckoned as nocturnal. The planet
Zuhra is the dancer of the heavens, and it rises in the third heaven. It is said and is the lesser of the auspicious planets.

The planet ʿUṭārid (Mercury) has a dry and cold nature. Its gender is female, and it is reckoned as diurnal. This planet is the scribe of the heavens, and it rises in the second heaven. It is mumtezij (composite/mixed) and is present in all four elements. The planet ʿUṭārid becomes good with the good and bad with the bad.

The planet Qamar (the Moon) has a moist and cold nature; its element is water, its gender is female, and it is reckoned as nocturnal. This planet is the physician of the heavens, and it rises in the first heaven. It is said and is the lesser of the luminous planets.

The planets Mushtarī and Zuhra are the Sa'deyn (the Two Fortunes). The planets Zuḥal and Mirrīkh are the Naḥsayn (the Two Misfortunes). The planets Mushtarī and Zuhra are [called] the ʿUlwiyyayn (the Two Superior Ones). The planets Zuḥal and ʿUṭārid are [called] the Suflīyayn (the Two Inferior Ones). The Sun and Qamar are [called] the Neyreyn (the Two Luminaries). When a planet joins with an auspicious planet it becomes auspicious, and when it joins with an inauspicious planet it becomes inauspicious — this condition is called mumtezij.

How the Basṭof the Letters Is Performed
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 37
Let us explain how the basṭof the letters (Basti Ḥurūfī) is carried out, from the first basṭto the fifth.

The basṭis performed in two ways: one by letters, the other by number-words. In both the basṭof letters and the basṭof number-words, the first basṭis the same. In the basṭof letters, the second basṭis obtained by summing the numerical values of the letters that make up the spoken form of the first basṭ. The third basṭis obtained from the sum of the second basṭ's numbers, the fourth [I 38] basṭfrom the sum of the third basṭ's numbers, and the fifth basṭfrom the sum of the fourth basṭ's numbers.

Let us explain the basṭof the letters by taking the letter Alif as an example, so that it may be more easily understood. Every letter, from Alif to Ye, is expanded (basṭ) in this same manner. The first, second, third, fourth, and fifth basts of the letter Alif are as follows:
First basṭ: the numerical value of the letter Alif is one (1); written out in the Arabic tongue, this is Ahad. We wrote out the word Ahad:
Dal, Ha, Alif.

We added up the numerical values of these letters, and it came to thirteen. The count of these letters is itself three (3). We added the two together and got 16. The first-basṭnumber of the letter Alif is 16.

Second basṭ: we performed istinṭāq (soyletmek, "to make speak" — the technique of converting a number back into the letters it corresponds to) on sixteen (16), the number of Alif's first basṭ. These letters emerged:
Ye, Wāw.
The way the numerical value of these letters is written out in the Arabic tongue is as follows:
Asherah, Sitteh.
Written as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ' (spelled out letter by letter):
He, Ra, Shin, ʿAyn, He, Te, Sin.
The numerical value of these letters is 60 + 400 + 5... We add the number 7 to 1040, giving 1047. This is the second basṭof the letter Alif.
Third basṭ: we performed istinṭāq on 1047, the number of Alif's second basṭ, and these letters emerged:
[I 39] Ghayn, Mīm, Ze.
The way the numerical value of these letters is written out in the Arabic tongue:
Alif, Erbeīn, Sebah.
Written as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ':
Alif, Erbaīn, Sebah.
Since this comes to 581, we add the number 13, giving a total of 594. This is the third basṭof the letter Alif.
Fourth basṭ: we took 594, the number of Alif's third basṭ, and performed istinṭāq on it. These letters resulted:
Se, Sat, Dal.
The way the numerical value of these letters is written out in the Arabic tongue is as follows:
Hamsemieh, Tisīn, Erbaah.
Written as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ':
Hamsemieh, Tisīn, Erbaah.
[I 40] Since this comes to seventeen (17) letters, we add the number seventeen (17) to 1624, giving 1641. This number is the fourth basṭof the letter Alif.
Fifth basṭ: we took 1641, the number of Alif's fourth basṭ, and performed istinṭāq on it. These letters emerged:
Ghayn, Khāʾ, Mīm, Alif.
The way the numerical value of these letters is written out in the Arabic tongue is as follows:
Alif, Sittemieh, Erbaīn, Ahad.
Written as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ':
Alif, Sittemieh, Erbaīn, Ahad.
Since this comes to 973, we add the number 18, giving a total of 991. This number, 991, is the fifth basṭof the letter Alif.

In this same manner, you expand (basṭ) the remaining twenty-seven (27) letters, following this same order. From each letter's first basṭ comes the second; from the second comes the third; from the third comes the fourth; and from the fourth comes the fifth.

[I 43] The Nine Mizans of the Basṭof the Letters His Eminence Shaykh Tamtam Samur Hindi (may God be pleased with him) gathered nine mizans (measuring standards) within the science of basṭ (the expansion/spreading method) and explained these nine mizans as follows.

First mīzān: you expand the letters of the names of the talib (the seeker, the one performing the working) and the maṭlūb (the object of the working), or of the name of the thing intended, taking them as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ' (the letters treated separately, each on its own).

Second mīzān: whatever the name of the talib and the maṭlūb, or of the thing intended, may be, you look to the elements (ʿanāṣir) of its letters. Having seen whether the letters are equal or not from the standpoint of their elements, whichever element's letters are the more numerous, you expand the letters of that element.
Third mīzān: if the working is by day, you expand the letters of the word "day"; if by night, the letters of the word "night," taking them as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ'.
Fourth mīzān: whichever hour you are currently in, you expand the letters of that hour as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ'.
Fifth mīzān: whichever day you are currently in, you expand the letters of that day as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ'.
Sixth mīzān: whichever planet belongs to that day, you expand the letters of that planet's name as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ'.
Seventh mīzān: whatever your need may be, you expand the letters of one of the four mizans (Jalb, Tard, Sihhat, and Sakam).
Eighth mīzān: if the working is for good, you expand the letters of the word "good"; if for ill, the letters of the word "ill," as ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ'.

[I 44] Ninth mīzān: you expand the degrees of the elements relevant to your need. If the working you are performing concerns fire, you expand whichever of the degrees of the element of fire suits your working. Having expanded these nine mizans, you total the numbers according to the first basṭnumber, and you interrogate (istinṭāq) the figure that results.

The fourfold awfāq that follow below pertain to the ʿAnāṣir Arbaʿa (the Four Elements). The first hane (cell) of the wafq is the miftah (key, starting point). What lies hidden within it is the abjad calculation. What matters most is to make the awfāq on the day and in the hour of the maṭlūb.

The rule for making a fourfold wafq: thirty (30) is subtracted from the number to be worked into the wafq, and the remainder is divided by four (4). The quotient is written into the first hane of the wafq, and by adding one at each step, one proceeds to the last hane until the wafq is complete. If the remainder of the division is three (3), one extra is added to the fifth hane; if the remainder is two (2), one extra is added to the ninth (9) hane; and if the remainder is one (1), one extra is added to the thirteenth (13) hane — in this way the wafq is completed. The fourth hane, however, is the secret of the wafq. Understand this well!
These are the awfāq of the ʿAnāṣir Arbaʿa:
[I 69] When you are about to begin a working, you must know well the day and the hour of your maṭlūb. A month has four weeks. Each ʿanāṣir has four degrees.
According to some scholars, however, the element of Water has five degrees.
First week: for love, affection, subjugation, intimacy, arousal, and attraction, you perform the basṭof the first degree of the ʿanāṣir.
Second week: for the fulfilment of a need, healing, and curing the sick, you perform the basṭof the second degree of the ʿanāṣir.
Third week: for binding the tongue, binding sleep, binding women and men, causing illness, or other bindings, you perform the basṭof the third degree of the ʿanāṣir.
Fourth week: for subjugation, ruin, separation, and enmity, you perform the basṭof the fourth degree of the ʿanāṣir.

If you act according to this rule, you will succeed by the permission of Allah (glory be to Him). If the ʿanāṣir of your maṭlūb is Earth, Air, or Water, you perform the basṭof the degrees of these elements in this same order. You must also know well the days on which the working is to be performed, so that whatever working you undertake will be free of error and will conclude in success.
On Sunday, Thursday, and Friday, the first hours at sunrise are for beginning beneficial workings.
On Monday and Wednesday, the first hours at sunrise are for binding the tongue, binding sleep, and binding virility.
On Tuesday and Saturday, the first hours at sunrise are for separation, subjugation, ruin, destruction, and enmity.

Take care that the conditions of these workings are neither incomplete nor deficient. If you perform them wrongly or in error, the working you have done will be in vain. You must perform them on the aforementioned days, at sunrise, in the first hours.

The Multiplication of Letters
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 105

This is the practice of taking the letters of the names of the petitioner (talib) and the object of the working, together with the letters of the name of the purpose (ḥāja), and, in a working of good or ill, arranging them (basṭ) into a single line (satri vahid); the letters of this line are then multiplied (taksir) until a terminal line (zimam satri) emerges.

For example, if we wish to make Hasan and Emel fall in love with one another, we arrange the letters of their names together with the word mahabba (love) in the following order, forming a single line ("satri vahid," a single line):

Lam Mīm Alif Be Ha Ye Nun Sin Ha We multiply the letters until the terminal line emerges. Once the terminal line has emerged, we write the multiplied letters, apart from the terminal line itself, onto a fine piece of leather or paper. Having written them, we take the first three letters from the right of the original line and the last three letters from its left. We then take the first three letters from the right of the line just before the terminal line, and the last three letters from its left. To each of these three-letter groups we append the word Ayil and bind them into names. We take the jummal value (the numerical value by the jummal reckoning, akin to abjad) of the original line, perform istinṭāq on this number, and append Ayil to the result. The name that emerges is the name of the spirit (rūḥānī) governing the four names. For each letter of this governing spirit's name, we take one of the Names of Allah, the Exalted, that begins with that letter. We write these Names of Allah, the Exalted, together with the conjuration (Qasam) we have composed beneath them, on the back of the paper on which we wrote the multiplied letters. Having written it, we hang the paper on a stick over the fire, light incense beneath it, and, while the incense burns, recite the conjuration in the following order.

Suppose the numerical value of the name of the spirit governing the four names is 351; then Allah [I 106] Teala, the Exalted — we recite His Names once, the conjuration once, the Names 50 times, the conjuration once, and the Names 300 times, the conjuration once more. Having recited it, if the predominant element is fire, we bury what we have written beneath or near a fire. If it is earth, we bury it at the maṭlūb's threshold or in a grave. If it is air, we hang it facing the wind or carry it upon our person. If it is water, we give its water to the maṭlūb to drink, or bury the writing beneath water.

To determine the predominant element, we look at the letters of the original line. Whichever element predominates, you proceed according to that element. If the letters of the original line are equal among the elements, you carry out your working according to whichever element you wish.
Some scholars have said: Air is the strongest of the elements, followed by Fire, then Earth, then Water.

If your working is one of ill intent and you wish to separate Hasan and Emel, you proceed as above, but instead of the word Ayil, you append the word Tishin to the end of the names. This is because in workings of good, celestial spirits (Ulwi arwah) carry out the operation, while in workings of ill, infernal spirits (Sufli arwah) carry it out. The names of celestial spirits end in Ayil, and those of infernal spirits end in Tishin. Let us give an example of this science of letter-multiplication, so that it may be better understood.

Twelve (12) is subtracted from the number for which the wafq is to be made, and the remainder is divided by three (3). The quotient is written into the first cell, and, adding one at each step, one proceeds to the wafq's last cell to complete it. Made this way, the threefold wafq admits no kasr (remainder).
The threefold wafq's planet is Saturn, and its day is Saturday.
Its celestial (ulwi) muwakkil (governing spirit) is Kesfeyail, and its terrestrial (arḍi) muwakkil is Meymun.

For example: let us make the threefold wafq of the Lafza-i Celal — the noble name Allah. We subtract twelve (12) from sixty-six (66), the numerical value of the noble name Allah (Almighty and Glorious), and divide the remainder by three (3).
The quotient is eighteen (18). Since no remainder is left, we write the quotient into the wafq's first cell and, adding one at each step, proceed to the ninth and last cell to complete the wafq.
This is the threefold wafq of the noble name Allah (Almighty and Glorious):

Among threefold and single-digit awfāq there are forms that admit a remainder and forms that do not. When the number to be made into a wafq is divided and the division leaves a remainder of one, adding that extra one to the seventh cell of the threefold wafq produces a deficiency of one in the left diagonal. If the remainder is two, adding the extra to the fourth cell produces an excess of one in the left diagonal. A wafq is correct when its edges, rows, and diagonals all come out equal no matter from which direction they are totalled. When they do not come out equal, a wafq made in this way is wrong.
